memories.content: Use the same term throughout the proposal for the same interaction concept or interface element.
Use abbreviations only for recurring terms of three or more words.
Present the full name and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Prioritize the research role over diagnostic labels or deficits when referring to participants.
Reviewers from different subfields struggle to infer undefined abbreviations from context alone.
Use the term formative evaluation for studies seeking design modification evidence, and distinguish it from final efficacy judgments.
The user can have contribution labels such as principles, models, or guidelines approved only if they align with the abstraction level of the actual deliverables.
Design principles describe the relationship between conditions and outcomes rather than serving as instructions that merely replicate a single screen layout.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

options.label: Same threshold
options.text: Treat “long” as three or more words, with the same rule applying to proposals generally.

options.label: Two-page scope
options.text: Treat the three-word threshold as the applicable interpretation specifically for two-page proposals.

options.label: Different standards
options.text: Treat “long” as a separate criterion that is not defined by the three-word threshold.

issues.question: For a two-page proposal, does “long recurring terms” mean every recurring term of three or more words, and is that threshold intended outside two-page proposals?
issues.title: Clarify abbreviation eligibility
issues.why_it_matters: The answer determines whether the policies are aligned, scoped by document length, or impose different eligibility standards on the same term.

analysis.overview: The frames align on terminology consistency, abbreviation expansion, participant framing, and cross-subfield readability. Abbreviation eligibility remains ambiguous because one frame supplies a word-count threshold while the other uses “long” within a two-page proposal. Each frame also contributes separate guidance in different areas.

relations.reason: Both prohibit mid-proposal terminology changes for the same referent; their listed referent categories differ but support the same naming policy without contradiction.
relations.summary: Use stable names throughout a proposal for entities or concepts that remain the same.

relations.reason: One frame sets a threshold of three or more words, while the other says “long” and explicitly mentions a two-page proposal; the payload does not establish whether these standards coincide.
relations.summary: Restrict abbreviations to recurring multiword terms, with differing descriptions of the qualifying length and document scope.

relations.reason: Both state the same first-use expansion requirement under the same abbreviation scope.
relations.summary: Give the full term together with its abbreviation at first use.

relations.reason: Both prescribe role-first participant terminology and reject status-centered framing under the same participant-reference scope.
relations.summary: Describe participants by their study roles rather than status-based, diagnostic, or deficit-oriented labels.

relations.reason: Both identify the same cross-subfield comprehension problem caused by relying on contextual inference for undefined abbreviations.
relations.summary: Reviewers across subfields cannot reliably infer abbreviations that have not been defined.

relations.reason: This is independently useful terminology guidance supplied only by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Reserve “formative evaluation” for studies seeking evidence to modify a design, distinct from final efficacy judgment.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only policy for selecting labels such as principles, models, or guidelines.
relations.summary: Approve contribution labels only when their abstraction level matches the actual deliverables.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only definition of the appropriate abstraction for design principles.
relations.summary: Treat design principles as relationships between conditions and outcomes, not instructions reproducing one screen layout.

relations.reason: This is independently useful role-definition guidance supplied only by the compared frame.
relations.summary: Define a newly introduced operational role by both its decision authority and its performed actions.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only claim about site-specific variation in operational authority.
relations.summary: Recognize that identical job titles can carry different modification and data-access privileges across deployment sites.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only observation about the user's role-labeling tendency.
relations.summary: Distinct field roles are liable to be collapsed under the generic label “user.”

reports.both: Both favor stable terminology, expanding abbreviations at first use, role-based participant descriptions, and avoiding undefined abbreviations that burden cross-subfield reviewers.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds operational-role definitions, site-dependent privilege distinctions, and a warning against collapsing distinct field roles into “user.”
reports.differences: Abbreviation eligibility differs between a three-or-more-word threshold and an undefined “long recurring terms” standard scoped to a two-page proposal.
reports.reference_only: The reference adds formative-evaluation terminology, deliverable-aligned contribution labels, and an outcome-oriented definition of design principles.
